utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Please be seated. May I ask Madam Registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Case number IT-02-61-PT, the Prosecutor versus Miroslav Deronjic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And may I have the appearances for the parties. For the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President and Your Honours, colleagues from the Defence. My name is Mark Harmon. To my right is Ms. Camille Bibles. To her right is Mr. Fergal Gaynor. We represent the Office of the Prosecutor in these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: For the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours; good afternoon colleagues from the Prosecution. I'm Slobodan Cvijetic, attorney-at-law and I'm Defence counsel for Miroslav Deronjic. Next to me is my colleague, also an attorney-at-law, Slobodan Zecevic, co-counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And my I finally ask, because this is a Status Conference -- scheduled as a Status Conference, first, Mr. Deronjic, can you follow the proceedings in a language you understand; and secondly, do you have any health problems in this very moment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can follow, Your Honour, the Status Conference in a language I understand, and I have no health problems at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated again. This morning, following a long conversation amongst the parties, a bunch of documents was filed, and this forms now the basis of the proceedings to follow. Especially we have to deal with a Plea Agreement, with an Amended Indictment, and with an additional Factual Basis. But I think it's only reasonable before we turn to these points to ask the Defence: There is still a motion pending on an alleged illegal arrest. What about this motion?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Defence withdraws this motion because we believe that it is unnecessary to rule on that motion at this point in time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I hear why this caveat "at this point in time"? Do you want to withdraw your motion without any condition or under condition?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We withdraw this motion. We give up on it altogether definitely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification. For purposes of transparency, it seems to be necessary that the Plea Agreement be read out in its entirety. I think we can delete the introduction, but please may I ask first the Prosecution and the parties having filed the motion confidential, are there any obstacles to lift the confidentiality?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, we would move that the seal on all of the three documents that have been filed be lifted at this point in time, and we would later make a motion to amend the existing indictment and have the Court accept the Second Amended Indictment in its place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Any objections by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. The Defence has no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The confidential -- confidentiality is lifted at the same time, Therefore, we can discuss it in open court, and may I therefore ask Madam Registrar please to read out the plea as such, terms of the agreement are as follows, and then continue with that what we can read in the Plea Agreement signed. Please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. The terms of the agreement are as follows: Plea. Miroslav Deronjic agrees to plead guilty to persecutions on political, racial, and religious grounds, a crime against humanity (hereinafter "persecutions"), punishable under Articles 5(h) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal (hereinafter "Statute"), as alleged in the Second Amended Indictment. A written Factual Basis supporting the crime of persecutions, punishable under Article 5(h) of the Statute and Miroslav Deronjic's participation in it has been prepared and filed with the Trial Chamber (hereinafter "Factual Basis"). Miroslav Deronjic has reviewed with his attorneys the Factual Basis. Miroslav Deronjic adopts the Factual Basis and agrees that he is pleading guilty to the charge of persecutions contained in the Second Amended Indictment because he is in fact guilty and acknowledges full responsibility for his actions that are described therein. Nature of the Offence. Miroslav Deronjic understands that the Prosecution would have had to prove each of the following elements beyond a reasonable doubt for him to be found guilty of persecutions: (a) the existence of an armed conflict; (b) the existence of a widespread or systematic attack directed against a civilian population; (c) the accused's conduct was related to the widespread or systematic attack directed against a civilian population; (d) the accused had knowledge of the wider context in which his conduct occurred; (e) the accused committed acts or omissions against a victim or victim population violating a basic or fundamental human right; (f) the accused intended to commit the violation; (g) the accused's conduct was committed on political, racial or religious grounds; and (h) the accused's conduct was committed with a conscious intent to discriminate. Penalty and Sentencing. Miroslav Deronjic understands that the maximum sentence that can be imposed by the Trial Chamber for a guilty plea to the charge of persecutions contained in the Second Amended Indictment is a term of imprisonment for a term up to and including the remainder of the convicted person's life as described in Rule 101(A). Miroslav Deronjic understands that the Trial Chamber shall not be bound by any agreement specified in Rule 62 ter (A) of the Tribunal's Rules of Procedure and Evidence. In determining the sentence, the Trial Chamber shall, pursuant to Article 24(2) of the Statute, take into consideration such factors as the gravity of the offence and the individual circumstances of the convicted person as well as those factors described in Rule 101(B): any aggravating circumstances; any mitigating circumstances including the substantial cooperation with the Prosecution before or after conviction; the general practice regarding prison sentences in the courts of the former Yugoslavia. Based on all of the factors and considerations mentioned in the preceding paragraph, the Defence will recommended to the Trial Chamber that it impose a term of imprisonment of no more than six years. Pursuant to Rule 101(C), Miroslav Deronjic shall be given credit for the period during which he was detained in custody pending the imposition of sentence by the Trial Chamber. Consideration by the Prosecutor. In exchange for Miroslav Deronjic's plea of guilty to the charge of persecutions contained in the Second Amended Indictment, the Prosecutor agrees to the following: (a) based on Miroslav Deronjic's full and substantial cooperation with the Office of the Prosecutor, the Prosecutor will recommended to the Trial Chamber that it impose a term of 10 years imprisonment. Miroslav Deronjic understands that the Trial Chamber is not bound to accept the Prosecution's recommendation and may impose a sentence above or below the Prosecution's recommended sentence. The imposition of such a sentence will not vitiate the plea of guilty; (b) the Prosecutor will take necessary and reasonable steps to ensure the safety and protection of Miroslav Deronjic and members of his family; (c) Miroslav Deronjic's guilty plea represents a full accounting of his criminal behaviour for the 9 May 1992 events in the village of Glogova; (d) the Prosecutor will advise any national domestic court regarding Miroslav Deronjic's culpability for any further crimes alleged in respect of the 9 May 1992 events in the village of Glogova as described in the Factual Basis and in the Second Amended Indictment that they have been dealt with by way of sentence provided by the Trial Chamber; (e) that the Prosecutor will advise any national domestic court regarding Miroslav Deronjic's criminal conduct in respect of the 9 May 1992 events in the village of Glogova as described in the Factual Basis and in the Second Amended Indictment that the Tribunal's Office of the Prosecutor has primacy over the prosecution of that crime; (f) no other promises or inducements have been made by the Prosecutor to induce Miroslav Deronjic to enter this agreement. Cooperation by Miroslav Deronjic. Miroslav Deronjic agrees to meet as often as necessary with members of the Office of the Prosecutor and to cooperate with and provide them with truthful and complete information that is known to him regarding individuals and events in the former Yugoslavia. He agrees to be truthful and candid and to freely answer all questions put to him by members of the Office of the Prosecutor. Miroslav Deronjic agrees to testify truthfully in any trials, hearings, and proceedings before the Tribunal where the Prosecutor deems his evidence may be relevant, whether those matters are presently before the Tribunal or may be in the future. Waiver of Rights. By pleading guilty, Miroslav Deronjic understands that he will be waiving the following rights in these proceedings: (a) the right to plead not guilty and require the Prosecution to prove the charges in the indictment beyond a reasonable doubt at a public trial; (b) the right to prepare and put forward a defence to the charges at such public trial; (c) the right to be tried without undue delay; (d) the right to be tried in his presence, and to defend himself in person at trial or through legal assistance of his own choosing at trial; (e) the right to examine at his trial, or to have examined, the witnesses against him or to obtain the attendance and examination of witnesses on his behalf at trial under the same conditions as witnesses against him; and (f) the right not to be compelled to testify against himself. It is understood that by pleading guilty, the accused does not waive his right to be represented by counsel at all stages of the proceedings. Declaration of Miroslav Deronjic. I, Miroslav Deronjic, have read this Plea Agreement which sets forth in its entirety the understanding of the parties and have carefully reviewed every part of it with my attorneys Slobodan Cvijetic, Slobodan Zecevic, and Catherine Baen. My attorneys have advised me of my rights of possible defences and of the consequences of entering into the agreement. No promises or inducements have been made to me other than those contained in this agreement. Furthermore, no one has threatened me or forced me in any way to enter into this agreement and I have entered into this agreement freely and voluntarily and am of sound mind. I understand the terms of this agreement, and I voluntarily agree to each of the terms. Dated this 29th day of September, 2003. Signed, Miroslav Deronjic. Declaration of Counsel. We, Slobodan Cvijetic and Slobodan Zecevic are counsel for Miroslav Deronjic. We have carefully reviewed every part of this agreement with our client. Further, we have fully advised our client of his rights, of possible defences, of the maximum sentence and the consequences of entering into this agreement. To our knowledge, our client is of sound mind and his decision is an informed and voluntary one. Dated this 29th September 2003. Signed, Slobodan Cvijetic, Counsel for Miroslav Deronjic, and Slobodan Zecevic, Counsel for Miroslav Deronjic. Other Agreements. Except as expressly set forth in this agreement, there are no additional promises, understanding or agreements between the Office of the Prosecutor and Miroslav Deronjic or his counsel Slobodan Cvijetic and Slobodan Zecevic. Signed, Miroslav Deronjic; Slobodan Cvijetic, Counsel for Miroslav Deronjic; Slobodan Zecevic, Counsel for Miroslav Deronjic; Carla Del Ponte, Prosecutor; Mark Harmon, Senior Trial Attorney; Camille Bibles, Trial Attorney.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May I now turn to you, Mr. Deronjic, being today the main person of these proceedings. Would you please stand up. My first question is: The agreement just read out, was it read to you in a language you understood, and did you understand all the terms of the agreements and the detail -- and all the detail, or do you have any additional questions?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the agreement was read out in a language that I understand. I have fully understood it in all its details. I am fully aware of the text of this agreement, and at this point in time, I have no objections in relation to this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I ask you, did you enter in the agreement voluntarily? Were there any inducements or promises given to you in this context?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have signed this agreement of my own free will. Nobody made any promises to me or any inducements except for what is contained in the document itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Finally, I have to alert you that under Rule 62 ter (B), the Trial Chamber is not bound by any agreement or recommendation by one of the parties, and it is your understanding, as it is in fact already laid down in the agreement but it has to be re-emphasised, that the maximum sentence that could be imposed is a term of imprisonment up to and including the remainder of your life under Rule 101(A). Did you understand this?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have understood that the Trial Chamber is not bound to accept what is written in this agreement, but even having that in mind, I voluntarily agreed to the agreement as it stands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. May I turn now to the Prosecution. First question: According to Rule 62 bis, I have to ask the Prosecution is there a sufficient factual basis for the crime and the accused's participation in it, either on the basis of independent indicia or even evidence or, as it reads in our Rules, "lack of any material disagreement between the parties about the facts of the case"?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, there is an independent factual basis to support this guilty plea both independently by extraneous evidence and by a Factual Basis that we have filed as one of the documents that is presently before Your Honours. The Factual Basis contains 47 paragraphs, nine pages long in English version, and each of those pages has been Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. signed and dated by Mr. Deronjic, and we would submit this factual -- written Factual Basis is the basis that is the support of this guilty plea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And an additional question: We have reason to ask you as well, are there any additional commitments by the Prosecution to Mr. Deronjic? We have to be aware, and we are following the proceedings in this Tribunal, and the name of Mr. Deronjic has been mentioned several times in the context of the Srebrenica massacre. Was there at any point in time or is there today any initial suspicion or even a strong suspicion warranting an indictment against the accused on a possible involvement in this, and is there in this context any commitment not to indict Mr. Deronjic for such a possible involvement in the Srebrenica massacre?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, the -- all of the promises that have been made to Mr. Deronjic are set forth in the Plea Agreement. There are no other promises made to Mr. Deronjic, no other agreements made with Mr. Deronjic or his counsel. In respect of the events in 1995 in Srebrenica, notwithstanding the fact that Mr. Deronjic's name may have come up in the context of other trials, an indictment against Mr. Deronjic for those events is not warranted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for these comments. The Trial Chamber convenes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: After having conferred, the Trial Chamber is satisfied that the requirements set out in -- under Rules 62 bis and 62 ter are met and therefore accepts this agreement. May we now turn to the indictment. First, Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President and Your Honours, we have filed a Second Amended Indictment this morning. There is on the record at this point an amended indictment, and we would move to have the Court substitute the Second Amended Indictment in place of the previous indictment that currently exists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber has carefully reviewed the changes in this indictment and has seen no obstacles to this, I -- may I first hear the Defence on this issue.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have received the Second Amended Indictment. We have no objections, and we waive our right to object. We accept the text as we have received it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber hereby grants leave to amend the indictment. So therefore the Second Amended Indictment, dates from yesterday, forms the basis of the now following proceedings. May I ask you, Mr. Deronjic, are you prepared to discuss the Factual Basis and to enter a plea today?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am prepared to discuss all these documents today and to enter a plea today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. We discussed how best to proceed, and it seems to be the best way to start with the Factual Basis, the Factual Basis being one primarily based on your own statements and, therefore, in part going even beyond the Second Amended Indictment. Can we proceed this way: That I will start now reading out the Factual Basis paragraph by paragraph, and if the content is correct, please answer this way, that you are in agreement. However, if there should be only the slightest detail not correct, please advise us. It reads in the Factual Basis: Miroslav Deronjic, son of Milovan, was born on the 6th of June, 1954 in the municipality of Bratunac, Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: From September 1990 to the end of April 1992, he was President of the Bratunac Municipal Board of the Serbian Democratic Party of Bosnia and Herzegovina (hereinafter "SDS").

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: He was appointed member of the SDS party Commission on Personnel and Organisation by the Executive Board on 6 September 1991.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is also correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Miroslav Deronjic was president of the Bratunac Crisis Staff from the time when it assumed authority from the Executive Committee of the municipality and the organs of the municipality -- Municipal Assembly from the end of April 1992 to the time of its transformation to a War Commission established by the Presidency of the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina in June 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, these data are also correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Miroslav Deronjic was appointed a member of War Commission of the Bratunac municipality.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Miroslav Deronjic became a member of the Main Board of the SDS in the summer of 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: On 14 to 15 October 1991, the Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina, without the participation of SDS deputies, passed a memorandum supporting the creation of a sovereign Bosnia and Herzegovina. The Bosnian Serbs were committed to the goal that all Serbs in the former Yugoslavia would remain in a common state. Following the decision of the Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina to support sovereignty, the Bosnian Serb leadership, including Radovan Karadzic, Momcilo Krajisnik, Biljana Plavsic, and Nikola Koljevic undertook steps to establish Serbian ethnic territories in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I agree that this information is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The Bosnian Serb leadership, including Radovan Karadzic, Momcilo Krajisnik, Biljana Plavsic, and Nikola Koljevic understood and intended that the creation of Serbian ethnic territories included division of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the separation and the permanent removal of ethnic populations from municipalities designated as Serbian, either by agreement or by force. The Bosnian Serb leadership knew that any forcible removal of non-Serbs from Serbian-claimed territories would involve a discriminatory campaign of persecution.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I agree that these facts are correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In order to ensure creation of Serbian ethnic territories, the Bosnian Serb leadership, in collaboration with members of the government of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, including Mihalj Kertes, and with units of the Yugoslav People's Army (hereinafter "JNA") and units of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Serbia, armed large segments of the Bosnian Serb population. The Bosnian Serb leadership coordinated with Serbian military, police, and paramilitary units within and without Bosnia and Herzegovina to achieve their objectives of establishing Serbian ethnic territories in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, these facts are also correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: At a meeting convened in Sarajevo on or about the 19th of December, 1991 presided over by Radovan Karadzic and attended by, among others, deputies of the Bosnian Serb Assembly and by presidents of the Municipal Boards, including Miroslav Deronjic, "strictly confidential" written instructions were disseminated to the attendees relating to the establishment of Bosnian Serb municipal governmental bodies in diverse municipalities in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The instructions, entitled "Instructions for the organisation and activities of the organs of the Serb people in Bosnia and Herzegovina in a state of emergency" and dated 19 December 1991, were directed to municipalities where Bosnian Serbs comprised either a majority of the population (Variant A) or a minority of the population (Variant B). The contents of these instructions were explained to the participants of the meeting by Radovan Karadzic. The instructions identified precise steps to be taken within the respective municipalities in order to establish Bosnian Serb control. The instructions described two distinct phases of action.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the facts in this paragraph are also correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Bratunac Municipality was a Variant B municipality. The steps described in the instructions for Variant B municipalities included the formation of Crisis Staffs and the formation of Serb Assemblies. Upon receiving these confidential written instructions, Miroslav Deronjic returned to the Bratunac Municipality where, under his leadership and direction, the Municipal Board immediately adopted and implemented the instructions. An SDS Crisis Staff was formed and Miroslav Deronjic was elected president. A Serb Assembly was established, and Ljubisav Simic was elected president of that organ.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, these facts are also correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In late February 1992, Goran Zekic, a member of the Bosnian Serb Republic Assembly from the adjacent municipality of Srebrenica and a member of the SDS Main Board, conveyed the order to implement the second phase of these instructions in the Bratunac Municipality and Miroslav Deronjic took positive and concrete actions to do so, including affirmative actions in the Bratunac Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, these facts are also correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Miroslav Deronjic subscribed unequivocally to the policy of creating Serb ethnic territories within Bosnia and Herzegovina and later to the use of force to remove non-Serbs from Serb designated territories. In his leadership capacity in the Bratunac Municipality, Miroslav Deronjic actively participated in efforts to transform the Bratunac Municipality into Serb ethnic territory and achieve the objective set forth by the Bosnian Serb leadership.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the facts set out in this paragraph are correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: As part of the process of ensuring that Bratunac Municipality would become ethnic Serb territory, "volunteers" from the SFRY with the cooperation of the SFRY authorities crossed the Drina River on the 14th or 15th of April, 1992, and entered Skelani (Srebrenica Municipality). Their purpose for entering Bosnia and Herzegovina was to assist the Bosnian Serbs in taking over power and forcibly removing Muslims from the area.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, these facts are also fully true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: On 17 April 1992, "volunteers" from the SFRY entered Bratunac and, at the Hotel Fontana their commander met with and issued an ultimatum to the leaders of the Srebrenica and Bratunac Muslim communities to surrender weapons and legal authority to Bosnian Serbs or suffer destruction at the hands of thousands of Serb soldiers who were amassed across the Drina River in Serbia. Following the acquiescence of the ultimatum by the representatives of the Muslim community, the Crisis Staff assumed political power in the Bratunac Municipality.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, these facts are also correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thereafter, efforts to ethnically cleanse the Bosnian Muslim population from the Bratunac Municipality were undertaken. The means used to effectuate the cleansing included the intimidation and random killings of Bosnian Muslims by, in quotation marks, "volunteers" and others, and the looting of Muslim homes and businesses. This activity resulted in an unknown number of Bosnian Muslims fleeing from the municipality of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, these facts are also correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Glogova was a Muslim village located in the Bratunac Municipality on the main road between the town of Bratunac and the town of Konjevic Polje. According to the figures from the 1991 census, the population of Glogova numbered 1.913. Of these residents, the census described 1.901 of them as Muslim, 6 as Serbs, 4 as Yugoslavs, 1 as a Croat, and one as "other."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I agree that these facts are true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Between the end of April 1992, and early May 1992, Miroslav Deronjic in his capacity as president of the Bratunac Crisis Staff, authorised the Territorial Defence (hereinafter "TO"), and the Bratunac police forces to disarm the Bosnian Muslim population in the village of Glogova. On at least three occasions during that period, Bratunac police forces and the TO working in concert with members of the JNA went through Glogova and secured weapons from the Bosnian Muslim population.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: On one occasion towards the end of April 1992, the Bosnian Muslim population of Glogova was directed to appear at a meeting at the community building in Glogova and directed to turn in their weapons. On or about 27 April 1992, the villagers of Glogova were told by Milutin Milosevic, chief of Bratunac police, that they would not be attacked because they had turned over their weapons.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I agree that these facts are also correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The disarming of the Bosnian Muslims in Glogova and other Muslim villages was an important element in ensuring and facilitating the permanent removal of Bosnian Muslims from Glogova, the town of Bratunac, Suha, Voljavica and achieving the objectives set forth by the Bosnian Serb leadership.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, these facts are correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Between the 21st and 23rd of April, 1992, a small JNA formation arrived in the Bratunac municipality. The unit was part of an armoured mechanised unit and was under the command of a JNA captain by the name of Reljic. Approximately 20 to 30 men were in the unit. The unit was part of a mechanised armoured brigade that was located in Sekovici.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, what is stated in this paragraph is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Captain Reljic planned and assisted in the disarming of Muslim villages in the Bratunac municipality. Captain Reljic's JNA unit, the TO, and the police would jointly participate in the disarming of the Muslim villages. Following the disarming of a Muslim village, the JNA and the police announced that the army would guarantee the safety of the residents. The disarming of Muslim villages continued until the 6th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, these facts are correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: A second group of "volunteers" from Serbia also arrived in Bratunac. The commander of this group of volunteers was an individual nicknamed "Peki." As soon as they entered Bratunac, they committed several murders of Muslims, including the owners of a restaurant in Bratunac and several Muslims from the suburban neighbourhood called Zljevice. They also engaged in widespread looting of Muslim property. The activities of the so-called "volunteers" were known to the Bosnian Serb leadership in Bratunac including the authorities of the Crisis Staff, the Bratunac police, and the TO. These activities created panic amongst the local population and resulted in an unknown number of Muslim residents fleeing from the Bratunac municipality. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, these facts are also correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The arrival of the JNA unit under the command of Captain Reljic and the arrival of the so-called "volunteers" from Serbia was agreed upon by the top leadership on the Republika Srpska and the SFRY.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree that these facts are also correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: On the 6th or 7th of May, 1992, and in furtherance of a plan to attack the village of Glogova, Miroslav Deronjic and Captain Reljic travelled to the village of Magasici from which point they were able to view the entire village of Glogova. The purpose of this visit was to reconnoiter Glogova in preparation of the attack on the village.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: On the 7th of May, 1992, the preparations for the attack on Glogova began, and it was agreed that the attack would commence within 48 to 72 hours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In the afternoon of 8 May 1992, Goran Zekic, a well-known and popular political figure in Bratunac, who was a member of the Bosnian Serb Republic Assembly from the adjacent municipality of Srebrenica, was killed near Srebrenica and his body was brought to the town of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, these facts are also completely correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Later the same day, at 2200 hours, the Bratunac Crisis Staff met principally about the events surrounding the death of Goran Zekic and with the operation to attack Glogova. Miroslav Deronjic presided over this meeting. The portion of this meeting dealing with the attack on Glogova was attended only by members of the Crisis Staff, Captain Reljic, Rasa Milosevic, commander of the Kravica Detachment of the TO, and another individual who was a member of the State Security of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, these facts are also correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: At this session of the Crisis Staff, Miroslav Deronjic made introductory remarks that included an announcement that the operation against Glogova would be carried out the following day. He explained the strategic significance of taking Glogova and said that the plan to create Serbian ethnic territory could not be implemented in the Bratunac municipality without taking Glogova first and transferring the entire Bosnian Muslim population from Glogova to non-Serb territory within Central Bosnia. He said that if there was no resistance from the Muslim residents of Glogova, all the Muslim residents should be brought to the centre of the town and transported by bus and truck out of the Bratunac municipality to Kladanj. He also stated that if everything went well within the Glogova operation, the operation to permanently remove Bosnian Muslims would continue in the following days in the town of Bratunac and the communities of Voljavica and Suha. Following the introductory remarks by Miroslav Deronjic, and a discussion about the Glogova plan, the Bratunac Crisis Staff adopted the plan.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the facts set out in paragraph 29 are entirely correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Miroslav Deronjic, with the specific intent to discriminate against the Bosnian Muslim residents of Glogova and Bratunac Municipality on political and religious grounds, ordered the attack on Glogova.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Miroslav Deronjic knew that the attack on Glogova and the forcible displacement of the Bosnian Muslim population from it was part of a widespread and systematic attack directed against the Bosnian Muslim civilian population within parts of Bosnia and Herzegovina designated as the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The attack on Glogova occurred within the context of an armed conflict within Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is also correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The decision to attack Glogova and to displace permanently its Muslim residents was done in order to further the plan to create Serb ethnic territories within Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Following the adoption of the plan to attack Glogova, the Bratunac Crisis Staff debated the issue of burning Glogova. Miroslav Deronjic said that while it was impossible to forecast the events in Glogova, some houses should be set on fire as a warning to the Muslims in order to spread panic and fear amongst them and part of the houses should be preserved for refugees. Miroslav Deronjic also said that if fighting erupted, he did not care what happened to the houses.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Captain Reljic informed the Bratunac Crisis Staff that the JNA would participate in the operation. Miroslav Deronjic urged Captain Reljic to fire a tank shell into a house at the initial stage of the attack in order to sow panic among the Muslim residents of the Glogova.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The attack on Glogova was a joint operation. The attacking forces were comprised of members of the JNA (Reljic's unit), the Bratunac TO, the Bratunac police, and paramilitary so-called "volunteers" from Serbia (herein "attacking forces"). Miroslav Deronjic coordinated and monitored the attack on Glogova.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the facts set out in this paragraph are correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Miroslav Deronjic participated in the military operation against Glogova. On the evening of 8 May 1992, Miroslav Deronjic and other Bosnian Serbs took positions on an elevated ridge above Glogova and remained there until the operation against Glogova commenced at 0600 hours on the morning of 9 May 1992. The role of Miroslav Deronjic and members of his unit was to interdict Bosnian Muslims fleeing from Glogova in the direction of Srebrenica and to prevent Bosnian Muslims from Srebrenica from coming to the assistance of the residents of Glogova. Miroslav Deronjic and others remained at their positions until about 1000 hours on 9 May 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the facts in this paragraph are completely correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Immediately after the commencement of the attack on Glogova, members of the attacking forces set fire to Bosnian Muslim houses and outbuildings. Miroslav Deronjic was aware of this as the smoke from the burning houses and outbuildings was clearly visible to him. He was informed by a hand-held radio that there was no combat or resistance and that everything was going according to plan. He did not intervene to prevent the additional burning of Bosnian Muslim houses.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: At approximately 1000 hours on 9 May 1992, Miroslav Deronjic and other members of the military unit with whom he was associated left their positions and descended in the direction of Glogova. When Miroslav Deronjic and others arrived at the edge of Glogova, they came about five to ten Muslim houses. After checking the houses to determine if any Muslims remained in them, and finding none, Miroslav Deronjic authorised soldiers to burn the houses and they were burned.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thereafter, Miroslav Deronjic and his companions came upon another five to six Muslim houses from which the occupants had fled. At that location were members of the Kravica detachment, including Nedjo, nicknamed "Djedura." Miroslav Deronjic encouraged Nedjo, nicknamed "Djedura" and his companions to set fire to these Bosnian Muslim houses.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: There was no resistance from the Bosnian Muslim residents of the village. During the attack on the village, members of the attacking forces murdered 65 unarmed residents of the village identified in Schedule A which forms part of the Second Amended Indictment. We will come to this later. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Paragraph 42: Miroslav Deronjic did not physically commit any of the murders of the 65 civilians identified in Schedule A. However, at the time he ordered the attack, given the purpose and the objective of the attack, the existing political climate and the units that were to participate in, it was foreseeable to him and he was prepared to take the risk that innocent Muslim residents of Glogova could be murdered as it was a consequence that was natural and foreseeable.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I agree that this statement is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: During the attack on Glogova and in fulfilment of the operational objective of the plan to permanently displace Bosnian Muslims from the Bratunac municipality, many Bosnian Muslim residents of Glogova, principally women and children, were forcibly displaced from Glogova.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: As a result of the attack on the village of Glogova on the 9th of May, 1992, 65 Bosnian Muslim residents of the village were murdered. The entire Bosnian Muslim population of the village was forcibly displaced and a substantial number of Bosnian Muslim residences in Glogova were razed to the ground. The mosque was also burned and destroyed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Miroslav Deronjic was invited to Pale to report on the events in Glogova on either the 10th or the 11th of May, 1992, and he travelled to Pale to attend a meeting to report about the events in Bratunac Municipality.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Present at the meeting in Pale held in a large conference room were Radovan Karadzic, Velibor Ostojic, and Ratko Mladic, and presidents of Crisis Staffs in the Republika Srpska. Miroslav Deronjic made his report to Radovan Karadzic, Velibor Ostojic, and Ratko Mladic, who were seated together at a table in the conference room. On the wall behind them were maps that identified the ethnic composition of portions of Bosnia and Herzegovina in various colours. Serb areas were designated by the colour blue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, all these facts are correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And then finally paragraph 47: Miroslav Deronjic reported that Glogova had been partly destroyed and torched to a large extent and that the Bosnian Muslim population had been forcibly removed. After making this report, those assembled in the conference room applauded him and Velibor Ostojic commented, "Now we can colour Bratunac blue." Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Let us now turn to the additional facts included in the Second Amended Indictment forming now the basis of our present proceedings. We can no doubt omit the introduction. It would read: The Prosecutor of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, pursuant to her authority under Article 18 of the Statute of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia (hereinafter "the Statute of the Tribunal"), charges: Miroslav Deronjic with persecutions, a crime against humanity as set forth below. And then it follows a description of Mr. Miroslav Deronjic. We have discussed this part already beforehand. Let us now turn to the General Allegations included in paragraphs 13 through 16. Here it reads, and I read it in context, all the four paragraphs: At all times relevant to this indictment, a state of armed conflict existed in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The persecutions charged in this indictment were part of a widespread and systematic attack on the civilian population, principally on the Bosnian Muslim population of Bratunac Municipality in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. From the end of April until 9 May 1992, Miroslav Deronjic was required to abide by the laws and customs governing the conduct of armed conflicts. The general allegations contained in these paragraphs 13 through 15 are re-alleged and incorporated into the charge of persecutions in this indictment. Then in the indictment, the individual criminal responsibility is described as follows in paragraph 2. May I first hear, these statements included in these four paragraphs, are they correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then it reads in paragraph 2: Miroslav Deronjic is individually criminally responsible pursuant to Article 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal for a crime punishable under Article 5(h) of the Statute of the Tribunal as alleged in this indictment, which he ordered and committed. By using the word "committed" in this indictment, the Prosecutor does not mean that the accused physically committed any of the crimes charged personally. "Committed" in this indictment refers to participation in a joint criminal enterprise. The objective of the joint criminal enterprise was the permanent removal, by force or other means, of Bosnian Muslim inhabitants from the village of Glogova in the municipality of Bratunac through the commission of crimes which are punishable under Article 5 of the Statute of the Tribunal. Miroslav Deronjic participated in the joint criminal enterprise as a co-perpetrator. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The crimes enumerated, paragraphs 30, 36, 37, 38, and 39. May I ask the Prosecution this context, is it on purpose that 35 is not included?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: 35, Mr. President, is merely a paragraph that identifies the total number of residents from the -- from the city of Glogova who were executed during the 9 May 1992 attack and identifies those individuals as being listed in Schedule A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So I take it it's on purpose and you are limiting this paragraph 4 to the crimes enumerated in paragraphs 30, 36, 37, 38, and 39 as described in the charge of persecutions in this indictment were within the object of the joint criminal enterprise and Miroslav Deronjic held the state of mind necessary for the commission of persecutions. The crimes enumerated in paragraphs 31 through 34 as described in the charge of persecutions were the natural and foreseeable consequences of the execution of the joint criminal enterprise and Miroslav Deronjic was aware that these crimes were the possible consequences of the execution of the joint criminal enterprise.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The joint criminal enterprise was in existence for a time period that included the period from the end of April 1992 to 9 May 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Numerous individuals participated in this joint criminal enterprise. Each participant, by acts or omissions, contributed to achieving the objective of the enterprise. Miroslav Deronjic worked in concert with the other members of the joint criminal enterprise, including members of the Territorial Defence of the municipality of Bratunac ("TO"), Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. members of the elements of the Yugoslav People's Army ("JNA"), members of the Bratunac police forces (also known as SUP, Secretariat of Internal Affairs), and members of paramilitary forces.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, these facts are correct as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The members of the TO who were members of the joint criminal enterprise included Momir Nikolic, Najdan Mladjenovic, Nenad Deronjic, Dragutin Takac, Dusan Zivanovic, Gojko (Zivojin) Radic, Zoran Mladjenovic, Milo also known as "Riba" and Milan Zaric. The members of the JNA who were members of the joint criminal enterprise included members of the Novi Sad Corps from Serbia, who were under the command of Captain Reljic. The members of the Bratunac police forces who were members of the joint criminal enterprise included Milutin Milosevic, chief of the Serbian SUP; Miladin Jokic, Vidoje Radovic, Dragan Ilic, Dragan Vasiljevic, Sredoje Stevic; his first name is unknown, Mr. Vuksic; and also Tesic, first name unknown. The identity of the members of the paramilitary forces who were members of the joint criminal enterprise is unknown.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I agree with what the Prosecution has stated, namely that the mentioned persons took part in this attack.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Miroslav Deronjic acting as president of the Crisis Staff of the municipality of Bratunac and in concert with other members of the joint criminal enterprise participated in the joint criminal enterprise in the following ways: Between the end of April and early May of 1992, Miroslav Deronjic, exercising de facto and de jure control as president of the Bratunac Crisis Staff over the TO and de facto control over the Bratunac police forces authorised the TO and Bratunac police forces to disarm the Bosnian Muslim population in Glogova. On at least three occasions during that period, Bratunac police forces and the TO working in concert with members of the JNA went through Glogova and secured weapons from the Bosnian Muslim population. On an unknown date near the end of April 1992, the Bosnian Muslim population of Glogova was directed to appear at a meeting at the community building in Glogova. At that meeting, the residents of Glogova were told to turn in their weapons. As president of the Bratunac Crisis Staff, Miroslav Deronjic was aware of and agreed to the plan to disarm the population of Glogova. On or about 25 April 1992, armoured personnel carriers (APCs), military trucks and police cars arrived in Glogova. Soldiers that were part of that convoy declared themselves to be members of the Novi Sad Corps from Serbia and had arrived in order to gather weapons. Najdan Mladjenovic of the TO was present with the group as well as the following Bratunac policemen: Milutin Milosevic, chief of the Serbian SUP; Miladin Jokic, Vidoje Radovic, Dragan Ilic, Dragan Vasiljevic, Sredoje Stevic, and Mr. Vuksic and Tesic, their first names are unknown. This group looked for weapons in Glogova and issued an ultimatum to the villagers that the weapons were to be handed in two days later. On or about 27 April, 1992, a group comprising approximately the same individuals described in subparagraph (c) returned to Glogova in order to collect weapons. Milutin Milosevic, chief of the Serb SUP, told the villagers that Glogova would not be attacked because they had turned over the weapons. Milosevic added that he was speaking on behalf of Miroslav Deronjic. On the evening of 8 May 1992, Miroslav Deronjic in his capacity as president of the Crisis Staff of the municipality of Bratunac, a position which gave him de facto and de jure control over the TO and de facto control over the police in the municipality of Bratunac, gave an order to attack the village of Glogova, burn part of it, and forcibly displace its Bosnian Muslim residents. Miroslav Deronjic was aware on 8 May 1992, that he was ordering the attack on an unarmed civilian village.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, all the facts from paragraph 8 are correct, and I agree with all of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In the early morning hours of 9 May 1992, members of the joint criminal enterprise, specifically members of the Bratunac TO, the Bratunac police, the JNA, and paramilitaries (hereinafter "attacking forces"), working in concert, surrounded the village of Glogova. Thereafter, the attacking forces entered the village on foot and took control over of the village. The Bosnian Muslim villagers who previously had been disarmed offered no resistance. The attacking forces then set fire to Bosnian Muslim houses, buildings, and the mosque, causing the wanton and extensive destruction of Bosnian Muslim dwellings, businesses, institutions dedicated to religion, and personal property in the village of Glogova. A substantial part of the village of Glogova was razed to the ground. Miroslav Deronjic was present during the attack on Glogova.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I should like to state that these facts are correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In respect of the killings that occurred in the village of Glogova on 9 May 1992 as set forth more fully in paragraphs 31 to 35, Miroslav Deronjic is individually criminally responsible under Article 7(1) for committing the killings.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I understand the nature of my responsibility on the basis of this particular count.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In Respect of the wanton and extensive destruction of Bosnian Muslim dwellings, businesses, institutions dedicated to religion, and personal property which occurred in the village of Glogova on 9 May 1992 as set forth more fully in paragraphs 36 and 37, Miroslav Deronjic is individually criminally responsible under Article 7(1) for committing and ordering this wanton and extensive destruction.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I understand the nature of my responsibility as it is described here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In respect of the forcible displacement of civilians from the village of Glogova on 9 May 1992, as set forth more fully in paragraphs 38 and 39, Miroslav Deronjic is individually criminally responsible under Article 7 for committing and ordering the forcible displacement of civilians.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I understand the nature of my responsibility presented in this paragraph as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Mr. Deronjic, for technical reasons, the tapes have to be exchanged. We have to make a short break now. May I ask, Madam Registrar, would it be sufficient to have a break of ten minutes? So the trial stays adjourned until five minutes to 2.00. --- Break taken at 1.45 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry for this technical necessity to have a break, but at the same time, it was the appropriate time for a break, because we now turn to the statement of facts included in the indictment, starting with paragraph 17. The municipality of Bratunac is located in Eastern Bosnia and Herzegovina and, according to the 1991 census, had a population of 33.619, of which 21.535 were Muslims, 11.475 Serbs, 223 Yugoslavs, 40 Croats, and 346 other nationalities. The municipality of Bratunac was of major significance to the Bosnian Serbs as it was one of the municipalities within the strategic arc that the Serbs needed to link the Serbian populations of Bosnia and Herzegovina to a contiguous Serbian state.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I agree with the facts presented in this paragraph, and I consider them to be correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In the spring of 1992, armed conflict between Serbs and non-Serbs broke out in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, including in the municipality of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this paragraph is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: As part of the conflict, Bosnian Serb JNA and paramilitary forces carried out widespread and systematic attacks on the civilian population of this region.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The municipality of Bratunac was taken over by Bosnian Serb forces on 17 April 1992, and a systematic effort was launched to disarm the Bosnian Muslim population of the municipality, which was completed by the end of April 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, these facts are also correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Prior to 9 May 1992, Glogova was a village located in Bratunac municipality, in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, a few kilometres from the city of Bratunac. There were about 750 houses in Glogova, which was a predominantly Bosnian Muslim village. In 1991, the total population of the village was 1.913 residents of whom 1.901 were Muslims, 6 Serbs, 4 Yugoslavs, 1 Croat, and 1 "other." Hereinafter for purposes of this indictment, the term "Glogova" refers to the Bosnian Muslim part of the village of Glogova.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I agree with the facts presented in this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In late April and early May of 1992, Bosnian Muslim villagers of Glogova were disarmed. On at least three occasions during that time frame, Bratunac police forces, the TO and the JNA went through Glogova and secured weapons from the Bosnian Muslim population. On an unknown date near the end of April 1992, the Bosnian Muslim population of Glogova was directed to appear at a meeting at the community building in Glogova. At the meeting, the residents of Glogova were told to turn in their weapons. As president of the Bratunac Crisis Staff, Miroslav Deronjic was aware and agreed to the plan to disarm the population of Glogova.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, these facts are also correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: On or about 25 April 1992, armoured personnel carriers (APCs), military trucks and police cars arrived in Glogova. Soldiers that were part of that convoy declared themselves to be members of the Novi Sad Corps from Serbia, and had arrived in order to gather weapons. Najdan Mladjenovic of the TO was present with the group as well as the following Bratunac policemen: Milutin Milosevic, chief of the Serbian SUP; Miladin Jokic, Vidoje Radovic, Dragan Ilic, Dragan Vasiljevic, Sredoje Stevic, and Messrs. Vuksic and Tesic. Their first names are unknown. This group looked for weapons in Glogova and issued an ultimatum to the villagers that the weapons were to be handed in two days later.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I agree with these facts; they are correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: On or about 27 April 1992, a group comprising approximately the same individuals described in paragraph 23 returned to Glogova in order to collect weapons. Milutin Milosevic, chief of the Serb SUP, told the villagers that Glogova would not be attacked because they had turned over the weapons. Milosevic added that he was speaking on behalf of Miroslav Deronjic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I agree that these facts are correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: On the evening of 8 May 1992, Miroslav Deronjic, in his capacity as president of the Crisis Staff of the municipality of Bratunac, gave an order to attack the village of Glogova, to burn part of it down, and to forcibly displace the Bosnian Muslim residents from the village. Knowing that the Bosnian Muslims in Glogova had been disarmed, Miroslav Deronjic was aware on 8 May 1992 that he was ordering the attack on an undefended village.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, these facts are also correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: On 9 May 1992, members of the Bratunac TO, the Bratunac police, the JNA, and paramilitary forces attacked Glogova. Members of the attacking forces set fire to the mosque and to Bosnian Muslim homes, warehouses, businesses, fields, and haystacks. Approximately 65 Bosnian Muslim persons from Glogova were executed during the 9 May 1992 attack. At the end of the attack, a substantial part of Glogova was razed to the ground. The attacking forces forced the Bosnian Muslim civilians from their homes and forcibly displaced them from the village of Glogova to other parts of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, these facts are also correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: What now follows is the concrete charge on persecutions. From the end of April to 9 May 1992, Miroslav Deronjic individually as president of the Crisis Staff of the municipality of Bratunac and in concert with other members of the joint criminal enterprise ordered and committed persecutions of Bosnian Muslims on political, racial and religious grounds in the village of Glogova in the municipality of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I agree that the facts set out in this paragraph are correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: From the end of April to 9 May 1992, Miroslav Deronjic as president of the Crisis Staff of the municipality of Bratunac, acting individually and in concert with other members of the joint criminal enterprise, perpetrated persecutions in the following ways: First, the attack on the village of Glogova. On the evening of 8 May 1992, Miroslav Deronjic, in his capacity as president of the Crisis Staff of the municipality of Bratunac, gave the order to the Bratunac TO to attack and to partially burn Glogova, an undefended village.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, these facts are correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In the early morning hours of 9 May 1992, members of the joint criminal enterprise, specifically members of the Bratunac TO, the Bratunac police, the JNA, and paramilitaries, working in concert, surrounded the village of Glogova. Thereafter, the attacking forces entered the village on foot and took control of the village. The Bosnian Muslim villagers who previously had been disarmed offered no resistance. Miroslav Deronjic was present during the attack on Glogova and entered the village after the assault. Miroslav Deronjic is individually criminally responsible under Article 7(1) for committing and ordering the attack on the village of Glogova.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the facts in this paragraph are correct, and the nature of my responsibility as described in this paragraph is something I understand and it's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Let's now turn to the killing of Muslim villagers from Glogova. Paragraph 31: During the gathering of the Bosnian Muslim villagers of Glogova from their homes, members of the attacking forces shot and killed Bosnian Muslim villagers Medo Delic, Seco Ibisevic, his wife Zlatija, and Adem Junuzovic outside their homes. Miroslav Deronjic is individually criminally responsible under Article 7(1) for committing the killings described in this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I agree that the facts set out in this paragraph are correct and I understand the nature of my own responsibility in connection with this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The first mass killing. During the course of the attack, members of the attacking forces executed a group of approximately nineteen Bosnian Muslim men on the main road near the centre of the village where the Glogova villagers were gathered. The first group of executed men included Dzafo Delic, Hamed Delic, Saban Gerovic, Serif Golic, Avdo Golic, Rifat Golic, Ismail Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Ibisevic, Salih Junuzovic, Alija Milacevic, Hajro (Hajrudin) Memisevic, Samir Omerovic, Fejzo Omerovic, Nezir Omerovic, Nevzet Omerovic, Camil Rizanovic, Jasmin Rizanovic, Mensur Rizanovic, Nurija Rizanovic, and Uzeir Talovic. Miroslav Deronjic is individually criminally responsible under Article 7(1) for committing the killings described in this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I agree that the facts set out in this paragraph are correct and I understand the nature of my responsibility in this respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Let me take the occasion and -- to extend my sincere apologies to the relatives of the victims mentioned in this indictment in case I mispronounce the one or other name. I try to do my very best but I am aware that I am not capable to pronounce all the names in the correct way, but I think it is of high importance and relevance that the names of those killed at that time are mentioned in open court. Let's turn now to the second mass killing, paragraph 33. After the execution of the group of Bosnian Muslims referred to in paragraph 32, members of the attacking forces ordered other Muslim villagers to carry these and other bodies to the river. After all of the bodies were dumped into the river, those Bosnian Muslim villagers who had been ordered to carry the bodies were lined up by the river and executed. This group includes Ramiz Cosic, Selmo (Selman) Omerovic, and Mehmed Ibisevic. Miroslav Deronjic is individually criminally responsible under Article 7(1) for committing the killings described in this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, again I agree that the facts set out in this paragraph are correct, and I understand the nature of my responsibility in connection with these facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Later during the attack on Glogova, members of the attacking forces gathered a group of approximately 20 Bosnian Muslim men by the market in Glogova. These Bosnian Muslim men were ordered to walk to the river where they were executed by members of the attacking forces on the order of Najdan Mladjenovic, a member of the Bratunac TO. This group included Seco Delic, Redjo Delic, Meho Delic, a Mr. Gusis, the first name is unknown. The same is true for Mr. Hasibovic. Dzevad Ibisevic, Ilijaz Ibisevic, Kemal Ibisevic, Muharem Ibisevic, Mujo Ibisevic, Mustafa Ibisevic, Ramo Ibisevic, Sabrija Ibisevic, Abid Junuzovic, Huso Junuzovic, Mirzet Omerovic, Selmo Omerovic, and Mensur Omerovic. Miroslav Deronjic is individually criminally responsible under Article 7(1) for committing the killings described in this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I state that I agree with what is set out in this paragraph, and I understand the nature of my responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: A total of 65 Bosnian Muslim residents from Glogova were executed during 9 May 1992 attack. The murdered individuals are those listed in Schedule A which is attached and made part of this indictment. The names of those victims not mentioned yet in the connection of the first, second, and third mass killings are, according to Schedule A, Alihromic Hajdar, Beganovic Vahid, Cosic Ramiz, Delic Seco, Delic Redjo, Dzafo Delic, Delic Hamed, Delic Meva, Gerovic Saban, Gerovic Ramiz, Gusis and Hasibovic, the first names are unknown. Ibisevic Jusuf, Ibisevic Osman, Ibisevic Refik, Ibisevic Seco, Ibisevic Zlatija wife of Seco, Junuzovic Adem, Junuzovic Banovka, Junuzovic Halid, Music Saban, Omerovic Nermin, Omerovic Elvis son of Nezir, Rizvanovic Mustafa, Sacirovic Mujo, and the first name is unknown Selimic. So this would conclude the entire list of the 65 Bosnian Muslims killed during this attack. This is correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The indictment continues as follows in paragraph 36: During the 9 May 1992 attack on Glogova, the attacking forces systematically set fire to the mosque and to Bosnian Muslim homes, warehouses, businesses, personal property, fields and haystacks.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, these facts are also correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Miroslav Deronjic was present during the attack on Glogova while members of the attacking forces wantonly destroyed Bosnian Muslim homes, businesses, and personal property. A substantial part of Glogova was razed to the ground. Miroslav Deronjic is individually criminally responsible under Article 7(1) for committing and ordering the destruction of Bosnian Muslim property described in paragraphs 36 and 37.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the facts set out in this paragraph are correct, and I understand the nature of my responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: On 8 and 9 May 1992, Miroslav Deronjic committed and ordered the forcible removal and displacement of the Bosnian Muslims of Glogova from the municipality of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the fact set out in this paragraph is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: On 9 May 1992, during and immediately after the attack on Glogova, members of the attacking forces forcibly displaced Bosnian Muslim civilians from the village of Glogova to other parts of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Specifically, the women and children who survived the attack were placed on buses and forcibly displaced to Muslim-held territory located outside of the municipality of Bratunac. Miroslav Deronjic is individually criminally responsible under Article 7(1) for committing and ordering the forcible displacement of Bosnian Muslim civilians described in this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the facts are correct, and I understand the nature of my responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The persecutions of Bosnian Muslim civilians, as alleged above, resulted in the killings of approximately 65 Bosnian Muslims, the forcible displacement of the Bosnian Muslim population from Glogova and the destruction of the village of Glogova.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, these facts are correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Let us now turn to your final plea. It is alleged that by these acts and omissions you, Mr. Miroslav Deronjic, ordered and committed persecutions, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(h) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I understand the nature of the responsibility described in the paragraphs of this indictment, and I plead guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, may we take to the record that the accused has pleaded guilty to persecutions, a crime against humanity, as set out in the Second Amended Indictment. You may be seated, please. The next step in the proceedings will be a sentencing hearing. May I ask the parties what is the time needed to prepare the sentencing hearing?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President and Your Honours, we would ask for a sentencing hearing that would occur at the end of January or the beginning of February.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Is it your intention to present additional witnesses or expert witnesses on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We would require a maximum of one day to present the Prosecution's evidence in respect of the sentence and in respect of the recommendation that we have made that's contained in the Plea Agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. May I put the same questions to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my learned friends, bearing in mind all the circumstances and the obligations of the Defence counsel in preparing for a sentencing hearing, we agree that the end of January would be the best time, and we also will need only one day to present our evidence as required in these cases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Is it foreseen that the accused intends to testify or to give any statement, because when having a Plea Agreement, we have no access to the personality, the family environment, the growing up, the socialisation of the accused, and of course we have to take into account these individual factors and, therefore, the Trial Chamber is confronted with the question whether or not, as it is custom in all domestic legislations, to order under Rule 98, sentence to a forensic examiner to compile a report on the accused, or is the point of view of the Defence that based on that what you will submit there will be a sufficient basis for the Trial Chamber to come to the necessary conclusions and to come to the appropriate sentence?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have already decided that along with the evidence we will present to the Chamber, the accused may personally make a statement about the circumstances of the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber has not discussed this matter yet. However, it's a time to ask the Defence, in case the Trial Chamber comes to the conclusion that a forensic examination would be needed, of course this can only be done based on the cooperation by Mr. Deronjic. Would you and would Mr. Deronjic in person consent to such, the work of a forensic examiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there will be no problems in cooperation, and I will ask my client about this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I feel called upon to answer this question. I have no objection to cooperating in this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this clear statement. Would it be feasible and appropriate for the parties that we schedule the sentencing hearing as follows: Starting the 27th of January, continuing in any event 28 January, but nobody knows what will happen and what is necessary, to have the 29th and 30th of January as reserve days? Would this be possible for you?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's quite acceptable to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, it is also acceptable to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Then it would only be consequent that we hereby order the parties to present their sentencing briefs no later than Thursday, December 18, 2003. We'll say two days before the Court recess. Any obstacles to this? I can see no obstacles.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No obstacles, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No problems, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Then hereby ordered, and we expect this be filed on this very Thursday, 18 December 2003. May I ask the parties, are there any other issues to be discussed today?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: There are no additional issues on behalf of the Prosecution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. The Defence has no additional issues to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. The trial stays adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: at 2.33 p.m.
